newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASEAN Regional Forum should play proactive role.
newsitem.headline: ASEAN Regional Forum should play proactive role.

text.p: Southeast Asia wants the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) to play an active role in preventing regional conflicts, Malaysian Foreign Minister Abdullah Ahmad Badawi said on Friday.

"ARF has emerged as the most important security forum in the region, and we are now thinking of moving it forward from just a CBM (confidence building measure) process into one of preventive diplomacy," he told reporters at the ASEAN-European Union (EU) ministers meeting.
"That's the next step we want to move ARF into and we are asking senior officials to look into it and come up with positive suggestions."

The ARF was initiated in 1992, allowing ASEAN -- Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam -- to discuss security issues with the United States, EU, Russia, China, Japan, South Korea, Australia, New Zealand, Laos, Cambodia and Papua New Guinea.
Malaysia will host the next ARF meeting in July after the annual ASEAN foreign ministers conference.

Abdullah said Malaysia raised the proposal during the ASEAN-EU dialogue, in the context of the principles of the ASEAN Declaration on the South China Sea, where overlapping claims on the Spratly Islands were of particular concern.
"If that can be carefully studied and can be taken as some of the principles that are endorsed, then we are certainly entering into a new phase of preventive diplomacy," he said.

Several Southeast Asian countries claim all or part of the Spratlys. China, which claims all the low-lying islets believed to sit over significant oil deposits, has opposed moves to discuss the issue in multilateral forums.
